title: Airport eSIM: 70% off for six minutes
scenario: A kiosk screen beside baggage claim advertises a “landing-only” eSIM deal with a six-minute countdown. The QR code installs a profile and asks you to sign in with your main email account to activate it.

answers.A: Buy or install an eSIM through a carrier or provider you independently choose, using its official app or site.
answers.B: Ask airport information whether the kiosk is an approved telecom seller before scanning anything.
answers.C: Scan it now but deny any permissions that look unrelated to mobile data.

explanation: A countdown can make an unknown profile feel routine. You should know who controls the software or profile before installing it.
proTip: Cheap data is not worth an unknown configuration profile.
